text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended higher on fund buying. March finished $28 higher at $1,558 per tonne, while May was up $27 also at $1,558 per tonne. The market was influenced by the strong performance in New York which was dominated by persistent speculative interest. On the physical front, traders said differentials for spot coffee had narrowed slightly as roasters rushed to plug nearby supply shortfalls. In New York arabica futures rocked up further gains but a rush of commission house profit taking knocked prices off fresh contract highs set earlier in the day. March ended 1.80 cents/lb higher at 147.45 cents/lb, while May was up 1.95 cents/lb at 142.55 cents/lb. Supportive for the market was buying in advance of a Colombian meeting tomorrow, which some fear could spark another strike. Other positive factors were falling certified coffee stocks and potential for both the Brazilian and Colombian crops to be lower in the 1997/98 season.

ICO - Coffee exports by exporting members of the International Coffee Organization fell to 6.34 million 60-kg bags in December 1996 from 6.78 million bags in November but up from 6.25 million bags in December 1995, the International Coffee Organization said. That brought total exports in calendar year 1996 up to 74.54 million bags from 67,00 million bags the previous year. In the first three months of the 1996/97 coffee year (October/December) exports reached 18.84 million bags, up from 17.51 million bags in the same 1995/96 period. NICARAGUA - Nicaragua's coffee growers have lowered their production estimate for 1996/97 (October/September) to 728,000 60-kg bags, down from an earlier forecast of 767,000 bags. Last year's production was significantly higher at 925,000 bags. Growers said that a lack of financing to fertilize crops, bad roads, armed gangs and a bout with leaf rust (La Roya) have hurt production.

POLAND - Poland imported 157,735 bags of coffee in July 1996, 28 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 939,800 bags, 7 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose to 1.536 million bags, up from 1.442 million bags the previous year. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Ivory Coast (117,700 vs 124,800 bags), India (109,000 vs 49,800 bags), Indonesia (182,800 vs 106,000 bags) and Vietnam (135,900 vs 174,600 bags). The country exported 47,100 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, up from 27,100 bags exported the same period in 1995.
